text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] KV cache amplification detected in us-west-prod shards — sustained read amplification and continuous-batch window growth causing gen-api tail-latency cliff. Pager: eng-oncall (P1). Link: https://dash.redwood/prod/kv_cache_amplification?from=now-30m

Maya Park: i'm on it. seeing error spikes + tail latency up to ~900ms on single-token responses for gen-api.

Ajay Johnson: which customers are hitting this hardest?

Maya Park: CUST-8425 and CUST-1994 stand out. their recent traffic shows heavy prefix reuse and KV page counts are inflating. batch-size autoscaler climbed to 512 in affected shards causing memory thrash.

Priya Shah: pinging @Kevin Li for deploy assistance. SLO breaches for gen-api routes confirmed.

Kevin Li: i can run a rapid mitigation: flip a global safeguard to cap batch size and apply a per-customer override to disable continuous batching for the worst offender. proposed commands: 

```
redwoodctl feature-flag set batching.safeguard_v2 true --scope global
redwoodctl customer-override set CUST-8425 batching.continuous false
redwoodctl rollout config set batch.max_size=64 --canary=2
```

Maya Park: agree. canary to 2 shards first. impact assessment: CUST-8425 ~12% traffic, CUST-1994 ~4% traffic.

Ajay Johnson: i'll prep temp probes and alerts against sample prompts for those customers. also creating an incident timeline entry.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: initiating canary rollout: 2% -> 10% -> 100%. watch windows: 2m per step.

Maya Park: flipped global flag `batching.safeguard_v2=true` (confirmed via feature service).

Kevin Li: applied customer override for CUST-8425. immediate signal: KV entries for their shard dropping, memory down ~22%.

Priya Shah: small note: expect op count to rise (smaller batches) but token throughput should be stable. request hold at 10% for 15m to observe stabilization.

Maya Park: also added temporary route fallback for high-latency traffic to `model-small` to avoid tail-latency blowouts while we monitor.

Ajay Johnson: notifying CS and sending brief note to affected customers: "We've applied an override to improve latency; we're continuing to investigate root cause."

Maya Park: at 10% canary, tail latency on probes improved from ~900ms -> ~160ms.

Kevin Li: proceeding to 100% per on-call consensus. running: 

```
redwoodctl rollout config set batch.max_size=64 --canary=100 --reason "KV amplification hotfix"
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout reached 100% in 45s. no rollout errors.

Priya Shah: metrics: per-route error rate stable, cost delta ~+3% due to smaller batches — acceptable for mitigation.

Maya Park: filing follow-up ticket RUNTIME-2741 "KV eviction/regression in continuous-batching path" with heap dumps and batch-sampler logs attached. assigning to eng-runtime.

Ajay Johnson: handoff note: i'm offline in 30m. @Maya Park please take primary for postmortem, next oncall -> @Kevin Li.

Kevin Li: taking handoff. i'll monitor dashboards for 2 hours and schedule a 30m check-in.

Maya Park: final customer-impact summary: CUST-8425 (12% traffic) latency improved avg 300ms -> 80ms after override; CUST-1994 (4%) improved 220ms -> 95ms. no data loss or dropped requests observed.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: marking incident state: mitigated.

Priya Shah: action items for post-incident review: 1) tighten batch autoscaling soft-caps and add hard ceilings, 2) improve KV cache eviction heuristics for long-prefix reuse patterns, 3) publish per-customer emergency-override runbook and playbook, 4) add canary probes for batch autoscaler regressions.

Maya Park: will paste relevant logs, flagged traces, and the customer notifications into RUNTIME-2741. marking this thread for retention.

Ajay Johnson: reactions: :thumbsup: great work, team."
